endorsements.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Device Software Functions: Lifecycle Management and Marketing Submission Recommendations (draft guidance)
endorsements.quote: When operating points are configurable, how end users can discern the operating650 point the device is currently operating at.

commentary.bottom_line: No supplied study tests whether showing users the active operating point or configuration of an AI device, with instructions on when to choose alternatives, reduces misinterpretation of outputs. The recommendation currently rests on a single FDA draft guidance that asks developers to explain how users can tell which operating point the device is using.

perspectives.view: The evidence base contains zero studies testing the practice and zero studies documenting the hazard. Under GRADE conventions, certainty cannot be rated above no direct evidence. The link between display of the operating point and fewer interpretation errors remains a plausible assumption that no supplied study has measured.

The FDA draft guidance on AI-enabled device software functions states that, when operating points are configurable, a submission should describe how end users can discern the operating point currently in use. Draft guidance is nonbinding, and the text addresses discernibility of the active setting more directly than instructions for selecting alternatives.

commentary.research_gap: Studies are needed that compare clinician interpretation accuracy, and downstream decisions, when a configurable AI device does or does not display its active threshold and guidance on alternative settings. Such studies should also first establish how often users misread outputs because they do not know the active configuration, since no supplied study documents the frequency of this hazard.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested the practice, so no evidence covers Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Health systems serving these groups have no information on whether configuration displays are understood by their staff or affect outcomes for their patients, and any displays should be checked for clarity in those settings.
